description: Insert-as-reference by opaque part_id, or every part of assembly_id (same ids). copy:true mints a new part id and sets copiedFrom. instance:true with the part_id of a row already in the open assembly adds another placement of that part (a part instance): the new row shares the script, run and undo history of its definition (edit any one and all rebuild from one run) and has its own id, name, pose and visibility; position is a rough block-out (default: staggered along +X). Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. A position, in an assembly of two or more parts, adds warning { code: "unjointed_part", part_id, hint } when the new row is in no joint; the call still succeeds. The result is { partId (the new row), instanceOf, added, partCount }; parts lists the row with instanceOf. Works on local and git assemblies. A path or name is unknown_part / unknown_assembly. Does not write git. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

assembly_id.description: Insert every part of this assembly as references.

copy.description: Mint a new part id and set copiedFrom (independent file).

instance.description: With part_id (a row of the open assembly): add another placement of that part. The new row shares its script, run and undo history (edit any one and all rebuild) and has its own id, name, pose and visibility. The result is the new row id; parts lists it with instanceOf.

name.description: Local: new part name (same as create_part)

part_id.description: Part surf-id to insert as a reference (same id).

position.description: instance:true only: rough block-out translation [x, y, z] mm of the new row. Default staggers along +X like a UI-created part. joint_create sets the final placement when the instance touches another part. A position in an assembly of two or more parts returns warning unjointed_part when the new row is in no joint; the call still succeeds.

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

name: insert_part
